entities.summary: Horvat Rimmon, or simply Rimmon, alternatively Khirbet Umm er-Ramanin, is an archaeological site in the southern Judean Lowlands in Israel. Located on a low hill about 500 metres (1,600 ft) south of Lahav, it preserves the remains of a Jewish village occupied from the late Second Temple period into the early Islamic era. The site is home to a large synagogue complex, which went through three main construction phases from the 3rd to the 7th century CE, as well as a cemetery of rock-cut tombs, a subterranean hiding complex, a mikveh and domestic structures, and several late Roman and Byzantine coin hoards.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The synagogue complex in Kobrin is significant for its well-preserved architecture and artifacts from the late Second Temple period to the early Islamic era, providing valuable insights into Jewish life during this time. Its discovery has shed light on the cultural and religious practices of the region.
